newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian growth stocks lag value stocks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian growth stocks lag value stocks.

text.p: A historical calculation of ASX/Russell style indices back to the start of 1991 shows the cumulative return of value style stocks has consistently outperformed the market while growth style stocks have lagged.

Introduced in June this year, the Russell/ASX indexes split three existing ASX indexes, the All Ordinaries, the ASX 100 and the Small Ordinaries into growth and value components to create six new indexes which seperately track their performance.
The Russell/ASX indexes calculate price to net tangible asset (NTA) multiples as a way of identifying value and growth.

Stocks are ranked from low to high and then separated into quartiles. First quartile stocks with a low price to NTA, below 1.6, are classed as all value style. Those ranked in the fourth quartile, above 3.3 are classed as all growth style.

"In the U.S. the experience has been growth stocks can lag value stocks for extended periods of time, then their catch up is remarkably swift," said Scott Donald, a client manager at Frank Russell Australia.

Speaking at a seminar on the style index conducted by the Securities Institute of Australia, Greg Vaughan, quantitative analyst for HSBC Asset Management, said one theory was that the catch-up period for growth stocks occurred when there was a scarcity of stocks offering growth potential.
"In Australia, a prime example of this theory has been Coca-Cola Amatil shares this year," he said.
